title: Incident-driven directional eval playbook and hotpath test expansion
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Summary: A recent config rollout changed two inference hotpaths (KV cache TTL and continuous-batching window) and coincided with a spike in downstream quality alerts for long-prefix generation on the open-model variant. Root cause analysis indicates a narrow class of prompt shapes plus specific cache TTLs exposed a tokenization/kv-cache alignment edge that leads to subtle token dropout in some beam/temperature combos. This ticket builds a repeatable, directional evaluation playbook and extends our smoke/regression test basket to cover the config permutations that triggered the incident.

Goals:
- Make it straightforward to reproduce the observed quality degradation with minimal infra (local/CI reproducer).
- Capture and triage failing examples for eval authors and model ops.
- Prevent future rollouts from changing the same hotpath surface without automated alerting and a minimal smoke that catches regressions.

Scope (what we'll deliver in this ticket):
1) Instrumentation: add a lightweight capture hook in the runtime that snapshots request+response token alignment for requests hitting long-prefix paths (>= 4096 tokens) and when KV cache TTL != default. Hook controlled by runtime flag and off by default.
2) Directional eval harness: a small harness that can replay captured traces with controlled permutations (ttl, batch_window_ms, quant_profile, auto-kernel-choice) and produces a diff report (per-sample token-level diff + summary metrics).
3) Reproducer generator: a script that synthesizes canonical long-prefix samples from failed traces, normalizes tokenization differences, and stores golden/reference outputs for CI.
4) Smoke-suite expansion: add CI-level smoke tests that run the directional harness for three prioritized permutations derived from the incident matrix. These tests must be cheap (N<=30 samples) and run on preflight/merge for runtime config changes and model rollouts.
5) Playbook and alerting: a short runbook with triage steps, dashboard links, and a Canary gate checklist for config rollouts touching cache/batching/quant paths.

Non-goals: full evaluation coverage for all models or exhaustive permutation search in this ticket (we'll scope to the hotpaths implicated by the incident).
acceptance_criteria:
- A runtime capture hook exists behind a flag and can be toggled in staging; captures include request text, token boundaries, model variant, config snapshot, and a short diff.
- Directional harness can replay at least three failing traces and reproduce a measurable quality delta (token-drop or score delta) deterministically on the same model binary.
- Reproducer generator produces normalized samples and commits 3 golden references to the eval fixtures repo.
- CI smoke test runs on PRs touching runtime config code and fails the PR if the harness detects a regression from golden references.
- Playbook doc (Confluence) with triage checklist, links to the incident postmortem, and a short note for release owners added.
- Owners and oncall for the new tests defined and documented.
tasks: Add runtime capture hook (flagged) and unit tests
Create directional-eval harness (replay & diff) and bench locally
Define three smoke permutations and add CI job (fast, N<=30)
Draft a short playbook and link to the postmortem dashboard
PRs and code review: runtime + harness + CI
Follow-up: plan wider rollout of directional harness to other model families
